## Scene 1.1 render architecture (summary)

Scene 1.1 is a **single main viewport** with **no SubViewport, no CanvasGroup, and no per-object outline shaders** on environment art. Compositing is done with `z_index` (world) plus a fixed **CanvasLayer post stack**.

```mermaid
flowchart BT
  BG["Background_1_1 Sprite2D\nz_index -100\nbaked PNG lines"]
  Noir["NoirPaletteOverlay\nlayer 90\nscreen pass"]
  Player["PlayerLayer\nlayer 100\nwhite sprite + ShadowOutline"]
  Scan["ScanlineOverlay\nlayer 105"]
  CRT["CrtPluginOverlay\nlayer 108"]
  UI["TopDialogueOverlay\nlayer 110"]

  BG --> Noir
  Noir --> Player
  Player --> Scan
  Scan --> CRT
  CRT --> UI
```

---

## 1) Key files

### Scene & control
| Role | Path |
|------|------|
| Scene root | `c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\scenes\Arc_1\1.1_SchoolExterior.tscn` |
| Scene toggles (noir/scanline/CRT on/off) | `c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\scenes\Arc_1\1.1_SchoolExterior.gd` |
| Camera (fixed X, vertical follow) | `c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\scenes\Arc_1\camera_follow_vertical.gd` |

### Environment art (where “outlines” come from)
| Role | Path |
|------|------|
| **Single baked background** — black ink lines are in the PNG, not generated at runtime | `c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\exports\Drawings\1.1_SchoolExterior.png` |
| Sprite node `Background_1_1` | in `1.1_SchoolExterior.tscn` (`z_index = -100`, `scale ≈ 0.33`) |
| Legacy tile assets (unused in current scene) | `c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\assets\background_tiles\1.1_*.png` |

### Post-process stack (production)
| Layer | Scene | Shader | Purpose |
|-------|-------|--------|---------|
| 90 | `scenes/fx/NoirPaletteOverlay.tscn` | `scenes/fx/noir_palette_filter.gdshader` | Luminance → inverted AXEL palette (dark strokes → red lines) |
| 105 | `scenes/fx/ScanlineOverlay.tscn` | `scenes/fx/overworld_scanline.gdshader` | Grain, scanlines, vignette, flicker |
| 108 | `scenes/fx/CrtPluginOverlay.tscn` | `scenes/fx/crt_plugin_overlay.gdshader` | Curvature, phosphor mask, vignette, **whole-frame chroma** |
| 110 | `scenes/ui/TopDialogueOverlay.tscn` | — | UI above CRT (font outline via Label theme) |

Supporting:
- `scenes/fx/noir_overlay_guard.gd` — hides noir in editor (`screen_texture` is white in editor viewport)
- `scenes/fx/white_sprite.gdshader` — forces player fill to white while keeping alpha

### Player outline (runtime, not environment)
| Role | Path |
|------|------|
| Duplicate scaled sprite behind player | `ShadowOutline` node in `1.1_SchoolExterior.tscn` |
| Setup/sync logic | `c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\scripts\Player.gd` (`modulate` black @ 0.55 alpha, scale 1.06) |

### Look-dev / style sweep (test-only prototypes)
| Role | Path |
|------|------|
| Variant matrix | `test/visual_style/variant_matrix.gd` |
| Overlay applier | `test/visual_style/style_overlay_applier.gd` |
| Capture harness | `test/visual_style/capture_scene_1_1_style_sweep.gd` |
| Edge-detect + outline shader (C1) | `test/visual_style/shaders/option_c1_poster_dither.gdshader` |
| RGB phosphor mask (D) | `test/visual_style/shaders/option_d_crt_display.gdshader` |
| Style reference doc | `plans/references/VISUAL_STYLE_OPTIONS.md` |

---

## Where environment outlines are “generated”

**They are not procedurally generated.** They are **baked black strokes** in `1.1_SchoolExterior.png`, then **reinterpreted at runtime** by the noir screen pass:

```13:31:c:\Users\valtt\OneDrive\Godot\AXEL\axel_project\scenes\fx\noir_palette_filter.gdshader
void fragment() {
	vec4 src = texture(screen_texture, SCREEN_UV);
	float lum = dot(src.rgb, vec3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114));

	// Contrast boost centered on midpoint to preserve dark line strokes
	lum = clamp((lum - 0.5) * line_contrast + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0);

	vec4 mapped = black_color;

	// Inverted AXEL mapping: dark strokes -> red, mid/high luminance -> black fill.
	if (lum < t0) {
		mapped = blood_red_color;
	} else if (lum < t1) {
		mapped = dark_blood_color;
	} else {
		mapped = black_color;
	}

	COLOR = vec4(mapped.rgb, src.a);
}
```

So “environment outlines” today = **thresholded dark pixels → solid red**, with `line_contrast` and `filter_nearest` guarding thin 1px ink at lower resolutions.

The **player** uses a separate system: a second `AnimatedSprite2D` (`ShadowOutline`), not screen-space edge detection.

---

## Render layers / viewports / groups

| Mechanism | Used in 1.1? | Notes |
|-----------|---------------|-------|
| Main viewport | Yes | 1400×900 (`project.godot`), content scaling enabled |
| SubViewport | **No** | Everything renders to root viewport |
| CanvasLayer | **Yes** | Primary compositing model (90/100/105/108/110) |
| CanvasGroup | **No** | No grouped outline passes |
| `visibility_layer` / 3D render layers | **No** | 2D scene only |
| Per-sprite materials on background | **No** | Plain `Sprite2D`, no shader |
| `z_index` | Yes | Background at -100; player at 20 within PlayerLayer |

**Critical layer split:** `PlayerLayer` is **layer 100**, above noir (90). Player is **not noir-filtered**; scanline + CRT **do** affect the player because they run at 105/108.

---

## 2) Constraints / risks for a global RGB-shadow outline on all art outlines

1. **No separate outline render target** — Environment lines are pixels inside one PNG. A “global outline effect” must use **screen-space edge detection** or **per-node duplication** (like the player), not a dedicated outline layer.

2. **Noir already owns outline color** — Dark strokes are remapped to `blood_red_color`. An RGB fringe added before noir gets quantized; added after noir must distinguish red line pixels from red fills/gradients.

3. **Player vs environment mismatch** — Player bypasses noir (white via `white_sprite.gdshader` + black `ShadowOutline`). A screen pass at layer 90 affects env only; at 108 affects player too but player lines are white-on-transparent, not red noir lines. Hard to get one uniform “RGB shadow on all outlines.”

4. **Thin-line fragility** — Background is scaled to ~33% of source art. Edge detection (see C1’s `edge > 0.35` threshold) can miss, double, or shimmer on sub-pixel strokes. Project already uses `filter_nearest` specifically to preserve ink.

5. **Stack interaction** — Scanline noise + CRT chroma (`chroma = 0.0025`) + phosphor mask already add RGB separation on the **whole frame**. Outline-only RGB shadow may look like “more CRT” or create muddy double-fringing.

6. **Prior experiment reverted** — Outline-aware CRT boost in `test/visual_style/shaders/option_a_crt_plugin.gdshader` was tried and reverted (2026-05-23 changelog): edge-boosted full-frame treatment was not kept.

7. **UI exclusion** — `TopDialogueOverlay` at layer 110 sits above CRT. Global passes below 110 won’t touch dialogue; passes intended to catch UI outlines would CRT-distort readable text.

8. **Editor blind spot** — `noir_overlay_guard.gd` disables noir in editor; `screen_texture` post effects don’t preview correctly in 2D editor. Must validate in running game / style sweep captures.

9. **Global scope vs corridor** — Scene 1.2 uses per-sprite locker shaders (`locker_palette_filter.gdshader`, `highlighted_locker_palette_filter.gdshader`) on layer 95. A global outline pass may behave differently across Arc 1 scenes unless unified.

10. **Performance** — Edge-aware passes need extra neighbor samples per pixel (C1 uses 4; outline-aware CRT used 8). Fine for 1400×900, but stacks with existing 3 full-screen passes.

---

## 3) Best insertion points (with tradeoffs)

### A) **`noir_palette_filter.gdshader` (layer 90)** — best for environment line look
**How:** On edge/low-lum pixels, output base red line + offset R/G/B fringe before or instead of flat `blood_red_color`.

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| Directly targets the stroke→red pipeline | **Does not affect player** (layer 100) |
| `line_contrast` already separates strokes | Fights carefully tuned `t0/t1/t2` / line-preservation work |
| Global for all noir scenes | Any mistake breaks all overworld/combat-adjacent noir users |

**Best when:** RGB shadow should match the **red ink line art** on backgrounds only.

---

### B) **New screen pass at layer ~95** (between noir and player)
**How:** Sample noir output; edge-detect; add RGB fringe; player draws clean on top.

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| Env-only fringe without touching player silhouette | Player `ShadowOutline` stays separate black — **not unified** |
| Doesn’t alter noir quantization logic | Another full-screen pass + ordering maintenance |

**Best when:** You want RGB fringe on **environment outlines only**, keeping player treatment independent.

---

### C) **`crt_plugin_overlay.gdshader` (layer 108) with edge-masked chroma** — best for unified composite look
**How:** Extend CRT (pattern exists in reverted test shader + C1 edge math): boost `chroma` only where `edge > threshold`.

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| Affects **player + environment** together | Edge mask also hits high-contrast fill boundaries, not just “art outlines” |
| Fits existing CRT stack on 1.1 | Dialogue (110) still excluded |
| Style sweep can A/B via `StyleOverlayApplier` | Already tried in spirit and reverted — risk of over-processed look |

**Best when:** RGB shadow is a **CRT-style chromatic fringe** on all high-contrast edges in the final image.

---

### D) **Replace noir with C1-style shader** (`option_c1_poster_dither.gdshader`, layer 90)
**How:** Use `replace_noir` stack mode from style sweep; explicit edge detect forces outline pixels to black (or recolor to RGB fringe).

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| Prototype already in repo | Replaces production noir, not additive |
| Explicit edge detection | Dither + scanline may conflict (noted in `VISUAL_STYLE_OPTIONS.md`) |
| Testable via capture harness | Player layer split still applies |

**Best when:** Willing to **change the core quantization model**, not just add fringe.

---

### E) **Per-asset: background material + recolor `ShadowOutline`**
**How:** Custom `canvas_item` shader on `Background_1_1`; change player `ShadowOutline.modulate` to RGB offsets (or multiple offset sprites).

| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| Precise, predictable | **Not truly global** — every new art asset needs wiring |
| No extra full-screen pass | Corridor/1.2 props need separate handling |
| Works at any scale if tuned per asset | Duplicates logic already partially in player |

**Best when:** Only 1.1’s single background + player need the effect, or art count stays small.

---

### F) **Art pipeline (bake RGB shadow into PNG)**
| Pros | Cons |
|------|------|
| Zero runtime cost; WYSIWYG | Not dynamic; re-export on changes |
| No layer/stack risk | Player still needs runtime solution |

**Best when:** Effect is static and art-driven.

---

## Practical recommendation

For **“global RGB-shadow on all art outlines”** in the current architecture:

1. **Environment:** Extend **noir** (A) or insert **layer 95 edge pass** (B) — these are the only stages that see background strokes before player overlay.
2. **Player:** Extend **`Player.gd` / `ShadowOutline`** (E) in parallel — screen passes alone won’t unify both.
3. **Validate:** Use `capture_scene_1_1_style_sweep.gd` + `style_sweep_1_1_linefix/` PNGs; avoid editor-only preview.
4. **Avoid** unmasked whole-frame chroma increases in CRT unless you want general RGB split, not outline-specific treatment.

If you want, I can sketch a concrete shader pseudocode path for option A vs C aligned to the existing uniforms — still in Ask mode, so implementation would need Agent mode.
